head.title: ISO 9001:2015 Certified Rubber Manufacturer | Margo, Nashik
head.description: Margo Rubber Products holds ISO 9001:2015, certificate 09111526A, for the manufacture of moulded rubber components in Nashik, India. Scope, surveillance cycle and what it does not cover.

sections.title: Hero
sections.live: LIVE H1 → ISO 9001:2015 Certified · subhead is accurate and well written · the certificate number is known and appears nowhere above the fold

fields.label: H1 — 2 lines
fields.note: 6 words · live is 3 · adds the product noun and the geo. “ISO 9001:2015 Certified” alone is true of tens of thousands of companies and carries no head term

fields.label: Subhead
paragraphs: Margo Rubber Products operates a documented Quality Management System audited and certified to ISO 9001:2015 under certificate 09111526A, issued by Integral Certification Ltd and valid to 21 February 2027. The certified scope covers the manufacture of moulded rubber components.
leads: Margo Rubber Products operates a documented Quality Management System audited and certified to ISO 9001:2015 under certificate 09111526A, issued by Integral Certification Ltd and valid to 21 February 2027.
marked: **Margo Rubber Products operates a documented Quality Management System audited and certified to ISO 9001:2015 under certificate 09111526A, issued by Integral Certification Ltd and valid to 21 February 2027.** The certified scope covers the manufacture of moulded rubber components.
fields.note: 40 words · live is 26 · certificate number, issuing body, expiry and scope all in the first two sentences. These are the four things a supplier-qualification auditor is looking for, and live they appear either as placeholders or not at all

fields.label: CTA
fields.note: One button, not two. Understand the Scope → #scope comes off with section 02 — its target no longer exists. Anchor must carry the /certifications prefix, not /#certificate

fields.label: Badge
fields.note: Certificate number added to the badge. A number on the badge is what turns it from decoration into something checkable

notes: Heading. Page’s only <h1>, two <span class="block"> children.
Keyword. ISO 9001 rubber manufacturer India resolves across H1 and subhead. This is a genuine buyer query — procurement teams filter suppliers by certification before anything else.

AEO. The subhead is the answer to “is Margo Rubber Products ISO 9001 certified, and what does the certificate cover?” — entity, standard, number, issuer, expiry and scope in forty words. Nothing else on the site is this dense with checkable facts.
Alt. alt="ISO 9001:2015 certification badge, Margo Rubber Products".

fields.label: Action
paragraphs: DELETE THIS ENTIRE SECTION FROM THE WEBSITE.

Remove the whole block — the eyebrow, the H2, both sub-headings, all seven bullets, the IATF paragraph and the closing audit note. No replacement copy is written for it and none should be invented. The page runs hero → certificate → manufacturing → quality system → documentation request, and loses roughly 877px.

One consequence to carry forward, because it does not go away with the section: this block is currently the only place on the site that addresses IATF 16949, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 at all. Deleting it does not license those claims elsewhere as held certifications — each now carries a client-instructed status with a target year, identical on all four pages. The IATF, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, RoHS and REACH entries on /products and /about must still be corrected to In Progress or removed, exactly as sheets 02 and 03 specify. Otherwise the site goes from stating a truth and contradicting it, to simply making the false claim.

The scope limit itself — certificate 09111526A covers moulded components only — is still required, and is carried in section 03 below as a correction to the certificate block, where an auditor reads it.

sections.title: Manufacturing & facility
sections.live: LIVE H2 → Manufacturing & Facility · five capability cards, all plausible and mostly sourced · two figures need confirming and one image has a placeholder caption

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: Our Nashik plant runs compression and transfer moulding, injection moulding, continuous-cure extrusion and rubber-to-metal bonding. Process parameters are controlled and recorded per batch under the ISO 9001:2015 QMS, with cure records retrievable per production batch.
leads: Process parameters are controlled and recorded per batch under the ISO 9001:2015 QMS, with cure records retrievable per production batch.
marked: Our Nashik plant runs compression and transfer moulding, injection moulding, continuous-cure extrusion and rubber-to-metal bonding. **Process parameters are controlled and recorded per batch under the ISO 9001:2015 QMS, with cure records retrievable per production batch.**
fields.note: 36 words · live is 26 · injection moulding added — it is on every other capability list on the site and missing from this one

fields.label: Cards ×5
rows: Automated hydraulic presses with closed-loop temperature and pressure control. Cure-time profiles logged per batch and retrievable.
CONFIRM press tonnage — live says 50–300 tonne, which is not in any source document
Continuous-cure extrusion for profiles, cord and tube. Section checked against the drawing at start-up and at defined intervals; hardness per batch. Not yet within the ISO certificate scope.
Surface preparation, bonding-agent application and cure documented with operator sign-off.
CONFIRM — bonded pads appear in the company profile, but bonding as a named line does not
Automated in-house mixing with traceability to raw material lots. Compound released on hardness and specific gravity before it reaches a press.
Mould and die design, cutting, maintenance and modification in-house. Tooling records held as controlled documents.
Strengthened — live understates this as “maintenance and minor modifications” when tooling is designed and cut here
fields.note: Card bodies 16–22 words, matching live. The tool room card is the one worth strengthening — in-house tooling is a genuine differentiator and this page describes it as if Margo only repairs moulds someone else made

fields.label: Image caption
fields.note: Replaces “Workers operating heavy machinery on the production floor” — that string is an alt-text description that has leaked into the visible caption. Alt should read alt="Compression moulding presses at the Margo Rubber Products plant, Nashik"

notes: The alt-text leak is a real bug, not a wording preference. A generic image description rendered as visible caption means the alt attribute and the caption are the same string — so the image has either no useful alt or a duplicated one. Separate them.
The extrusion scope note carries the page’s honesty forward. Naming which line is outside the certificate, on the card describing that line, is the same move as the scope paragraph in section 02.
Heading levels. <h2> + five <h3> card titles.
Schema. None. The Place node for the plant ships from the homepage.
Internal links. Three: /products/extrusion, /products#compounds, /about#manufacturing. The live section has none.

sections.title: Quality system in practice
sections.live: LIVE H2 → Our Quality System in Practice · four stages, all sourced and correctly described · the intro line “no marketing language, just the actual process” earns itself

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: ISO 9001:2015 is a framework. Below is how it operates on the floor at Margo Rubber Products — no marketing language, just the actual process.
marked: ISO 9001:2015 is a framework. Below is how it operates on the floor at Margo Rubber Products — no marketing language, just the actual process.
fields.note: Unchanged. 25 words, and the page delivers on it

fields.label: Stages ×4
rows: All raw materials and bought-out parts sampled against acceptance criteria. Non-conforming lots quarantined and tagged. Release authorised before production use.
Defined control points at mould setup, first-off inspection and mid-production sampling. Dimensions, hardness and visual attributes verified per control plan.

Continuous visual and flash inspection at the press and after deflashing. Dimensional sampling per AQL plan. Hardness and specific gravity per batch. Signed inspection release data accompanies every despatch lot.
Customer complaints and internal non-conformances trigger documented root-cause analysis and corrective action. Effectiveness verified at closure. Records retained.
fields.note: (no change — keep the live wording) · (no change — keep the live wording) · (no change — keep the live wording) · Two edits in stage 3. “100% visual inspection on all moulded parts” becomes the process the profile actually documents — continuous visual and flash inspection at the press and after deflashing. A 100% claim is refutable by one escaped defect, and the real process is more specific anyway. “inspection record” becomes inspection release data, matching sheets 02, 05 and 06 — “record” and “certificate” both imply document classes that invite requests Margo cannot meet

fields.label: Audit note
paragraphs: For supplier qualification audits: we can provide our Quality Manual, process flow diagrams, control plans and FMEA documentation on request, under NDA where required. On-site quality and supply-chain audits are welcomed, not negotiated around.
marked: **For supplier qualification audits:** we can provide our Quality Manual, process flow diagrams, control plans and FMEA documentation on request, under NDA where required. On-site quality and supply-chain audits are welcomed, not negotiated around.
fields.note: 35 words · live is 40 · the closing clause is lifted from the company profile and is a stronger statement than anything else in this block. CONFIRM that FMEA documentation exists — it is named in the live copy and appears in no source document · CONFIRM

notes: Four named process stages with real control points is exactly what a second-party auditor searches for before booking a visit, and no competitor in the teardown publishes it.
Heading levels. <h2> + four <h3>.

“100%” claims are a category of risk. The site carries several — 100% safety record, 100% traceable, 100% recyclable packaging, 100% visual inspection. Each is refutable by a single counterexample, and none is measured. Where the underlying process is real, describe the process.
Cross-link. Stage 3 links to /products#testing where the twelve ASTM and ISO test standards are listed.
